prompt: A stranger downloads the shop's customer list. Which property of that list was lost?
hint: Who saw it, and who should have?

choices.text: Integrity, because the list is no longer in the shop's control
choices.why: The list was not changed. Integrity is about correctness.

choices.text: Confidentiality
choices.why: Right. It reached people it was not meant for.

choices.text: Availability, since the shop has one copy fewer
choices.why: The shop's copy is still there and still usable.

choices.text: Authenticity of the customers
choices.why: Nothing was claimed falsely about where data came from.

prompt: A script rounds every price in the catalogue to the nearest real. Nobody outside saw anything. What was damaged?
hint: The data is still private and still reachable.

choices.text: Nothing, because it was an accident and not an attack
choices.why: Integrity is lost by accidents as well as by tampering.

choices.text: Availability
choices.why: The catalogue is still online and answering.

choices.text: The integrity of the prices
choices.why: Right. They are no longer correct.

choices.text: Confidentiality, since the script read the prices
choices.why: Reading by an authorised script is not a disclosure.

prompt: Match each event at the shop to the property it damages.

pairs.left: A laptop with the payroll file is stolen
A supplier's bank account is changed in the system

prompt: A power cut takes the shop's only server down for two hours. Which properties does it threaten?
hint: The section names what a power cut does and does not touch.

choices.text: Confidentiality and availability
choices.why: Nobody reads anything because the power went out.

choices.text: All three, since the server is down
choices.why: Nothing was read or changed while it was off.

choices.text: Availability
choices.why: Right. The data is intact and private, and nobody can use it.

choices.text: Integrity, because the database was not shut down cleanly
choices.why: That is a possible side effect, and the section's answer is availability.

prompt: The three properties confidentiality, integrity and availability are called the ___ triad.
sha256sum -c prices.sha256 printed prices.csv: OK. What does that establish?

choices.text: That nobody has read the file since the hash was taken
choices.why: Reading changes nothing in the file, so a hash cannot see it.

choices.text: That the prices in it are correct
choices.why: A wrong price saved before the hash was taken passes too.

choices.text: That the file is byte for byte what it was when the hash was saved
choices.why: Right. It compares against the fingerprint kept from before.

choices.text: That the file came from ana
choices.why: A plain hash says nothing about who wrote the file.

prompt: After one character changed, the new hash began 350f6313 and the old one 6fff9e30. Why is it useful that they look nothing alike?
hint: Think about somebody trying to fake a file that passes.

choices.text: It makes the hash easier to read aloud
choices.why: Readability is not the point of a hash.

choices.text: It tells you which line changed
choices.why: A hash never points at the change; it says only that there was one.

choices.text: A nearly identical file will not pass the check
choices.why: Right. Small changes scramble the whole output.

choices.text: It shrinks the file so the check is faster
choices.why: The file is unchanged by hashing it.

prompt: An intern can edit both prices.csv and prices.sha256 in the same folder. What does the check now prove?

choices.text: Nothing against the intern: they change the file and its hash together
choices.why: Right. The kept fingerprint has to be safer than the file.

choices.text: That the intern did not change the prices
choices.why: They could update the hash to match the change.

choices.text: The same as before, since SHA-256 is strong
choices.why: The strength of the function does not help if the reference is writable.

choices.text: That any change made by someone outside the company would show up
choices.why: Anyone who can write to the folder can do what the intern can.

prompt: In the lab, curl printed exit 7 after the portal was stopped. What did that number mean?
hint: The section says it in words.

choices.text: The page was found but was empty
choices.why: No page came back at all.

choices.text: It could not connect at all
choices.why: Right. Nothing was listening on the server.

choices.text: The server refused to show the page to ana
choices.why: A refusal would be a reply; there was no reply.

choices.text: The page had changed since the last request
choices.why: curl has no idea of the previous request.

prompt: The portal was stopped and restarted, and nothing was read or changed. Why does the course still call that a security failure?

choices.text: Because the restart was done by root
choices.why: Who restarted it is not the issue.

choices.text: Because it might have been an attacker
choices.why: The cause does not decide it; a failure loses availability too.

choices.text: Because availability was lost, and that is one of the three
choices.why: Right. Every sale in that window was lost.

choices.text: It is not one; the course calls it an operations problem
choices.why: The section says the opposite.

prompt: A shop promises 99.9% availability over a 30-day month. How many minutes of downtime does that allow? (Round to the nearest minute.)
Match each cause of downtime to the defence the section pairs with it.
The shop encrypts its order database. What new availability risk does it take on?
hint: What does it need every time it reads its own data?

choices.text: Losing the key locks the shop out of its own data
choices.why: Right. Keeping the key available becomes somebody's job.

choices.text: Encrypted data is slower to steal
choices.why: That is not an availability risk to the shop.

choices.text: Customers can read their orders
choices.why: Encryption does not open the data to anybody.

choices.text: The data's integrity is lost
choices.why: Encrypting does not make the data incorrect.

prompt: Which property matters LEAST for the shop's public price list?

choices.text: Integrity, since anyone can see a wrong price and report it
choices.why: A wrong price costs money on every sale before anybody reports it.

choices.text: Availability
choices.why: Customers need it to buy.

choices.text: Confidentiality
choices.why: Right. Every visitor sees the prices already.

choices.text: All three matter equally for every file
choices.why: The section ranks them per piece of information.

prompt: Why do many systems slow down repeated wrong passwords instead of locking the account after three?
hint: Who else can type three wrong passwords?

choices.text: Locking costs more disk space
choices.why: Storage is not the concern.

choices.text: A lockout lets anybody who knows a username lock its owner out
choices.why: Right. It trades confidentiality for availability.

choices.text: Slowing down is stronger against guessing
choices.why: Both resist guessing; the difference is who else they hurt.

choices.text: Three is too few for a strong password
choices.why: Password strength is not what decides the count.

prompt: An email says it is from the bank and is not. Nothing in it was altered after it was written. Which property fails?

choices.text: Integrity
choices.why: Nothing changed on the way.

choices.text: Availability of the bank
choices.why: The bank is unaffected.

choices.text: Confidentiality of the message
choices.why: It reached the person it was sent to.

choices.text: Authenticity
choices.why: Right. It did not come from where it claims.

prompt: The shop's three administrators share one admin account. Nobody misuses it. Which property is already lost?
hint: When something goes wrong, what question cannot be answered?

choices.text: Accountability
choices.why: Right. Nobody can say which of the three did what.

choices.text: Availability, since one account is a single point of failure
choices.why: Three people can all use it; availability is not the loss.

choices.text: Privacy of the administrators
choices.why: Privacy concerns the people the data describes.

choices.text: Nothing, as long as the password is strong
choices.why: A strong shared password still cannot tell the three apart.

prompt: Match each CIA property to its DAD failure.
A company keeps its customer list perfectly confidential and uses it to sell the customers' reading habits to advertisers they never agreed to. What fails?

choices.text: Confidentiality, since the data reached advertisers
choices.why: The company chose to send it; the failure is about the person described.

choices.text: Integrity of the reading habits
choices.why: Nothing was altered.

choices.text: Privacy
choices.why: Right. A use the customer never agreed to.

choices.text: Non-repudiation of the sale
choices.why: Nobody is denying anything.

prompt: Order the steps the course gives for checking a file's integrity with a hash.
hint: The fingerprint has to exist before the change.
items: compute the hash of the file while it is known to be good
keep the hash somewhere the file's editors cannot write
later, compute the hash of the file again
compare the two and investigate any mismatch
trap: Without a fingerprint taken while the file was good there is nothing to compare with.

prompt: Which of these protect availability? Choose all that apply.
hint: Is the system still usable when something fails?

choices.text: A second server that takes over
choices.why: Redundancy.

choices.text: A backup that has been restored in a test
choices.why: A restorable copy brings the data back.

choices.text: A SHA-256 hash of the price list
choices.why: That detects changes: integrity.

choices.text: Encrypting the customer list
choices.why: That protects confidentiality, at some cost to availability.

prompt: A ransomware attack encrypts the shop's server and the attackers also copy the customer list first. Which properties were lost?

choices.text: Confidentiality and availability
choices.why: Right. The copy is a disclosure; the encryption is a denial.

choices.text: Availability
choices.why: The copy taken first is a second loss.

choices.text: Integrity, since the files were changed by encryption
choices.why: The course's DAD table puts ransomware under denial; the copy adds disclosure.

choices.text: Confidentiality
choices.why: The shop also cannot use its own server.
